article.title: Concept Drift: When the Relationship Your Model Learned Stops Holding
article.why: Practical analytical English with higher-difficulty emphasis.

paragraphs.en:
A production model can fail even when the distribution of its input features appears stable. This happens because predictive performance depends not only on what inputs look like, but also on the relationship between those inputs and the target. When that relationship changes, the system experiences concept drift.

Imagine a credit-risk model that learned that frequent salary deposits strongly predict repayment. The distribution of salary-deposit frequency may remain almost unchanged for months. However, if a new labor-market shock causes income stability to weaken, the same deposit pattern may no longer carry the same information about future repayment. The feature has not drifted much, but its meaning relative to the target has changed. A fraud model can face the same problem when criminals adapt to detection rules. A marketing model can deteriorate after a competitor changes prices, even if customer demographics remain stable.

Concept drift is different from ordinary data drift. Data drift usually refers to a change in the distribution of model inputs: customers become older, transaction amounts rise, or a new product generates unfamiliar categories. Data drift can matter, but it does not necessarily imply performance loss. If the predictive relationship remains stable, a shifted input distribution may still be handled well. Conversely, concept drift can damage performance without producing a dramatic shift in input histograms.

Detecting concept drift is difficult because the true target often arrives with delay. A churn model may not know whether a prediction was correct for several months. Credit default labels can take even longer. Teams therefore need layered monitoring. First, monitor input quality and distribution. Second, monitor score distributions and operational outcomes. Third, when labels arrive, evaluate discrimination, calibration, error rates, and segment-specific performance over time. Changes in calibration can be an early clue that the conditional relationship has shifted.

Retraining is not a universal cure. If the label definition changed, the pipeline broke, or the business policy altered who receives an outcome, simply fitting the same model on newer data may reproduce the problem. Analysts should investigate the mechanism: Did customer behavior change? Did the environment change? Did the target definition change? Did an upstream system modify a feature? Did the model itself alter the population through previous decisions?

Temporal validation is essential. Random train-test splits can hide drift because both sets contain the same historical mixture. A more realistic evaluation trains on the past and tests on a later period. Rolling windows can show how quickly performance decays. Segment-level analysis may reveal that the relationship changed only for certain products, regions, or customer types.

The operational response should depend on the diagnosis. Recalibration may be enough when ranking remains good but probabilities shift. Partial retraining may work when recent data captures the new relationship. Feature redesign may be necessary when an old proxy loses meaning. In some cases, the organization may need a new target or decision rule.

Concept drift matters because models are historical artifacts deployed into changing systems. Monitoring only whether features ‘look similar’ is not enough. Teams must ask whether the mapping from information to outcome still holds, and whether the decision process built around the model is still appropriate. The distinction also matters for feature engineering. A feature can preserve its marginal distribution while its conditional relationship with the target changes. For example, the proportion of customers using automatic payment may remain stable, yet a regulatory reform could change which customers benefit from that feature. Monitoring only population stability indices or univariate drift metrics would miss the change. Interaction effects can drift too: age may remain predictive overall while the relationship reverses within a newly introduced product.

Concept drift can be gradual, sudden, recurring, or seasonal. Gradual drift appears when behavior slowly evolves, such as customers moving from branch banking to mobile services. Sudden drift can follow a regulation, price shock, pandemic, fraud strategy, or major product redesign. Recurring drift appears when patterns return in holidays or annual renewal cycles. The monitoring strategy should reflect these dynamics. A single monthly alert threshold may be too slow for sudden fraud adaptation but too noisy for long-term credit behavior.

Label delay creates a serious operational challenge. If the true outcome arrives six months later, teams cannot wait for perfect evidence before reacting. Proxy monitoring can help: changes in score-to-action conversion, approval rates, manual-review findings, early delinquency, or customer complaints may provide warning signals. But proxies must be treated as diagnostic clues rather than substitutes for eventual outcome validation.

Model governance should define what happens after a drift alert. Teams need an investigation playbook rather than an automatic retraining button. First confirm data integrity: schema changes, missing values, unit conversions, timestamp bugs, and upstream system changes can imitate drift. Next determine whether population composition changed. Then evaluate outcome relationships when labels are available. Finally choose among recalibration, threshold adjustment, feature redesign, retraining, or model replacement.

There is also a feedback-loop problem. Once a model changes who receives loans, offers, investigations, or support, future labels are generated under that policy. Apparent concept drift may partly reflect the organization’s own interventions. Logging model version, score, action, eligibility, and override reason is therefore essential for diagnosis. Without that history, teams may be unable to distinguish market change from policy change.

The deeper lesson is that model monitoring is not merely a statistical dashboard. It is a process for maintaining a valid mapping between data, prediction, action, and outcome as the surrounding system evolves. A model can remain technically healthy while becoming strategically irrelevant, or look statistically different while still supporting good decisions. Effective monitoring asks not only whether distributions changed, but whether the model’s meaning changed.
paragraphs.zh:
【擴充翻譯】Concept drift 指的是『feature 與 target 之間的關係變了』，它與單純 input distribution 改變的 data drift 不同。例如薪資入帳頻率的分布可能幾乎沒變，但景氣衝擊使得同樣的薪資模式不再代表相同的還款能力；此時 feature 看起來穩定，model 的 predictive meaning 卻已改變。詐欺手法適應規則、競爭者改價或制度變更，也都可能造成類似情況。

因此，只監控 PSI、feature histogram 或 missing rate 不夠。concept drift 可能是 gradual、sudden、recurring 或 seasonal，甚至 interaction effect 也會漂移。真正麻煩的是 label delay：churn、default 等 outcome 要幾個月後才知道，團隊不能等到完整 label 才反應。此時 score distribution、manual review 結果、early delinquency、complaint 等可以做早期 diagnostic signal，但不能取代最終 outcome validation。

發生 alert 後也不應自動 retrain。先排除 schema change、unit conversion、timestamp bug、upstream change 等 data quality 問題，再確認 population、feature、score、label relationship 與 business policy。若 ranking 還好但 probability 偏掉，可能只需 recalibration；若 proxy 的意義已變，則需要 feature redesign；若 target 本身改了，甚至要重新定義 model。

更深一層是 feedback loop：model 會改變誰取得貸款、優惠或審查，因此之後的 label 本身就是在舊 policy 下生成的。要能診斷，必須記錄 model version、score、action、eligibility 與 override reason。model monitoring 的核心不是『分布有沒有變』，而是 data→prediction→action→outcome 的關係是否仍然有效。
paragraphs.ja:
【拡張訳】Concept driftとは、featureの分布そのものではなく、featureとtargetの関係が変化することを指す。たとえば給与振込頻度が以前と同じ分布でも、景気shockによって同じ振込patternが返済能力を示さなくなれば、inputは安定して見えてもpredictive meaningは変わる。fraudの適応、競合価格変更、制度改正でも同様のことが起こる。

そのためPSIやfeature histogramだけのmonitoringでは不十分である。driftにはgradual、sudden、recurring、seasonalな形があり、interactionも変化し得る。さらにlabel delayがあるため、churnやdefaultでは正解が判明するまで待てない。score distribution、manual review、early delinquency、complaintなどを早期signalとして使えるが、最終的なoutcome validationの代替ではない。

alert後に自動retrainingするのも危険である。schema変更、missing、unit conversion、timestamp bugなどdata qualityを先に切り分け、その後population、feature、score、label relationship、business policyを確認する。rankingが保たれprobabilityだけずれているならrecalibration、proxyの意味が変わったならfeature redesignが必要になる。

さらにmodel自身が誰にactionを与えるかを変えるため、将来labelは過去policyの影響を受ける。model version、score、action、eligibility、override reasonを記録し、data→prediction→action→outcomeの関係全体をmonitorすることが重要である。
